questions.q: What counts as a MAJOR version bump for a shared pipeline template, according to this lesson?
options: Fixing a typo in a log message produced inside the template
Renaming or removing an input, making a previously optional secret required, or changing a job name that branch protection depends on
Adding a new optional input with a default value
Updating the CHANGELOG.md file for a release
questions.explain: A MAJOR bump signals a breaking change — anything that changes the template's existing contract in a way an unmodified consumer can't survive.

questions.q: What does keeping a moving v1 tag alongside exact tags like v1.4.0 let consumers do?
options: Nothing — moving tags aren't supported by GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps
Skip semantic versioning entirely
Force every consumer onto the newest major version automatically
Choose between auto-picking up non-breaking v1.x improvements or freezing on one exact, known-good version
questions.explain: A repo calling @v1 gets every non-breaking improvement automatically, while a repo pinned to @v1.4.0 stays frozen until it deliberately changes that line.

questions.q: What happens if someone edits a pipeline template's main branch directly with no version discipline in place?
options: Every repo still pointed at @main breaks simultaneously on its next run, with no warning
Nothing changes for any consumer until they manually re-pull the template
GitHub or Azure DevOps automatically reverts the change
Only the template repo itself is affected, never its consumers
questions.explain: Without version pinning, every repo pointed at the moving branch inherits the change immediately and simultaneously, which is exactly the failure mode semantic versioning prevents.

questions.q: Which of these is a MINOR version change to a pipeline template?
options: Removing a required secret
Renaming an existing input
Adding a new optional input with a default value that existing consumers don't have to use
Changing a job name referenced by a consumer's branch protection rule
questions.explain: A MINOR release is backward-compatible — a new optional input with a sane default doesn't force any existing consumer to change anything.

questions.q: What problem does a CHANGELOG.md solve for teams depending on a shared pipeline template?
options: It automatically upgrades every consumer to the latest version
It replaces the need for semantic version tags
It enforces required security scans inside the pipeline itself
It lets a team self-serve whether it's safe to upgrade, without filing a support ticket
questions.explain: A changelog updated with every tagged release is what lets a consuming team assess upgrade risk on their own, rather than asking the platform team directly.
